findings.claim: CHECKLIST 'arms_running' is green with detail '5 running: tp-7pct, hold-12h, entry-8pct, sl-5pct, vol-4x'
findings.problem: The arena listing shows seven arms in state running/confirm — the five named plus control and placebo — so the checkbox's own count does not match the arm table it is meant to validate. Either control and placebo are running and are being undercounted, or the count is drawn from a different field than the status shown in the arena rows. A green check whose number disagrees with the underlying table does not establish the condition it claims.

findings.claim: entry-8pct is reported as [running/confirm] alongside the other arms
findings.problem: It has live_n=3 and screen_n=496 against control's screen_n=1550, and it is the only variant arm whose screen_ev is negative at -0.055 with screen_dWR=0.0pp. It sits in confirm on a materially smaller and non-shared screen population than the arms it will be compared against, while the paired_population check asserts every arm has seen all 4814 events. Those two statements cannot both be describing the same evidence base.

findings.claim: 'paired_population — Every arm scored on identical events: 4814 events in the shared window; every arm has seen all of them'
findings.problem: The per-arm still-open counts listed cover only control, hold-12h, placebo, sl-5pct, tp-7pct and vol-4x — entry-8pct is absent from that dictionary despite being a running/confirm arm. Its screen_n=496 and vol-4x's screen_n=866 also differ from the 1550 the other arms carry, which contradicts 'every arm has seen all of them' unless 'seen' means detections offered rather than events scored. The check is green on a definition that is not the one the promotion comparison needs.

findings.claim: Screen-stage results such as sl-5pct screen_dWR=5.29pp on screen_n=1549 are carried in the arena as the standing evidence for arms now in confirm
findings.problem: Those screen numbers come from the backfill tier (4764 backfill events vs 50 live), and the backfill_cannot_promote check confirms no arm has been promoted from a screen. The arena nonetheless presents screen_wr and screen_dWR as the headline statistic per arm with no live counterpart beyond live_n, so the visible ranking of the fleet is entirely backfill-derived while the stated rule is that only live-tape evidence can promote. The display invites a verdict the evidence tier forbids.

findings.claim: Arms are accumulating toward 'confirm planned n=600' at a 'measured ghost arrival = 25.2 control trades/day'
findings.problem: After a 62.0-day data span the confirm arms show live_n of 12 or 13, not a count consistent with that arrival rate over any meaningful confirm period. The 25.2/day figure is quoted for ghost arrivals while live_n counts scored trades, and nothing in the data reconciles the two, so the planned n=600 has no stated time-to-completion that the reported live_n supports. A rate quoted in one unit is being used to justify a target measured in another.

findings.claim: 'kernel_agreement — Kernel finds the same setups as the live bot: 195/200 live setups reproduced (97.5%)'
findings.problem: The events-by-tier line reports only 50 live events, so a comparison against 200 live setups is drawn from a population larger than the live tape this context reports. The five listed misses are also concentrated in two names, four of them BOME, which is a systematic pattern rather than the random shortfall a percentage-agreement threshold assumes. The 90% floor is passed on a number whose denominator is not reconciled with the live event count.
